trust_decision.summary: Before any AST-derived value is written into generated JavaScript it must be a literal of exactly its declared type (string for parts/keys/content/original-derived params, non-negative integer for depth, number for NumberLiteral, boolean for BooleanLiteral, array for pairs and blockParams); the decision is made at the compiler boundary in the node handlers of lib/handlebars/compiler/compiler.js, not by the shape check in lib/handlebars/compiler/base.js.

landing_point.why: The advisory is a bypass of CVE-2026-33937, whose fix is exactly validateAstNode/isValidDepth here; an engineer who reads only the summary opens this function to see which node values it fails to cover.

fix_sites.entry_point: Handlebars.parse / Handlebars.parseWithoutProcessing with a pre-parsed AST (reached from Handlebars.compile and Handlebars.precompile via env.parse)
fix_sites.module_kind: parser/AST entry wrapper (the check is deleted here and moved to the compiler)
compiler: Hash handler (pairs array, pair keys)
compiler: classifySexpr (helper-name parts read before the PathExpression handler)

fix_sites.entry_point: Handlebars.compile, Handlebars.precompile (incl. stringParams and trackIds option modes)
fix_sites.module_kind: compiler: pushParam, reads value/original/depth before accept()
error type: tolerate a partial loc instead of masking the message

O3_reason_to_dismiss: JavaScriptCompiler is a subclassable opcode consumer that never sees an AST node (its header calls the overridable methods a PUBLIC API), and its loc field is metadata, so a solver can argue the AST trust boundary ends in the Compiler and leave the generator alone.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate ASTs must keep compiling: parsed templates with very long numeric literals yield Infinity and NaN, hand-built or JSON-reloaded ASTs routinely omit depth and loc, and in stringParams mode number/boolean params must still be emitted as raw literals so helpers receive 0/false rather than '0'/'false'. The pinned check's isFinite test and its requirement that depth exist reject the first two.

O6_input_shapes: PathExpression.parts: not an array (string), array containing a number or a nested array
PathExpression.depth: string '0', negative, fractional, and absent (must default to 0)
PathExpression.depth reached through a param in stringParams mode, and path.parts read in trackIds mode before the node handler runs
NumberLiteral.value: string, array, or other non-number, in both normal and stringParams mode
Hash.pairs: not an array; HashPair.key: non-string
Program.blockParams: object carrying a code-bearing length instead of an array
param 'original' (bare path param in stringParams mode) that is not a string
node loc absent or partial (start only)
non-finite NumberLiteral values (Infinity) that must be accepted

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The exported low-level pipeline: new Handlebars.Compiler().compile(ast, options) followed by new Handlebars.JavaScriptCompiler().compile(env, options, undefined, true) produces template code from an AST without ever calling Handlebars.compile/precompile, so the base.js AST check never runs at the pinned commit.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Compiler and JavaScriptCompiler are exported plumbing that precompile() uses internally; the documented entry points are compile/precompile, so an application assembling the pipeline itself is on its own.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, lib/handlebars.js -> lib/handlebars/compiler/compiler.js:50-76 -> lib/handlebars/compiler/javascript-compiler.js:64; 2 files from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A derived-attribute helper that reads path.original or path.parts before the node handlers validate them, as simpleId/scopedId already do.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: classifySexpr calls simpleId first, which is exactly why the published fix had to hoist validateParts to the top of classifySexpr; a maintainer adding another predicate here would recreate a read-before-validate site.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Another raw string interpolation of a compiler value into generated source, like contextName's 'depths[' + context + ']'.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The generator assembles code by concatenation in pushId, programExpression and contextName; a maintainer adding an emitter for a new opcode would interpolate an AST-derived number or name the same way and trust the compiler to have checked it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A post-check AST rewrite that writes node values which the compiler later emits (omitLeft/omitRight already rewrite ContentStatement.value).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The pinned check runs before this pass, so any new whitespace rule that synthesises node values would put content on the emission path after validation has already run.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A new pushLiteral-style opcode that passes its argument straight to pushStackLiteral.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: pushLiteral is the sink for NumberLiteral/BooleanLiteral; a maintainer adding a literal node type (bigint, regexp, raw) would follow the same trusted-literal pattern.

O9_family: code injection (CWE-94) through AST type confusion (CWE-843) in generated JavaScript

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Extend validateAstNode in lib/handlebars/compiler/base.js:44-92 with StringLiteral, ContentStatement, Hash and blockParams cases while keeping the isFinite and depth-must-exist rules: it closes the shapes named in the report but breaks Infinity literals and depthless ASTs and never runs on the exported Compiler pipeline.
